paragraphs: The Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead delivers fostering in partnership with Achieving for Children, a not-for-profit fostering service owned by the Royal Borough together with Kingston and Richmond. It is shown above with the independent agencies that list Windsor and Maidenhead as an area they cover. Carers who foster through the council's service are first in line when a local child needs a home, for emergency, short-term or long-term care.

In March 2025 the council reported that its fostering agency had been rated good in every area by Ofsted after a week-long inspection that February. It also said that, from April 2025, it had strengthened its package for carers registered with Achieving for Children, which includes council tax reimbursement, a weekly fostering fee, a child allowance paid at the London rate, and training and support.

The council describes one-to-one support for each carer alongside group and team support, and a package of financial, practical and emotional help. Details of who can foster and how the approval process works are set out on the council's fostering page and in Achieving for Children's fostering brochure.

If you live in or near the Royal Borough, talk to the council's service and to two or three of the agencies above, and ask each what it pays, what training it gives and how it supports carers day to day before you choose.
